nodes.name: CoFe-PBA NS@NF synthesis
nodes.procedure: Note that before performing the in-situ coordination reaction, the purchased nickel foam was carefully treated several times with ethanol, acetone and deionized water to remove the surface impurities. 100 mL of an aqueous solution containing Na2Fe(CN)5NO·2H2O (1.0 mmol) was added and mixed with 100 mL of an aqueous solution containing Co(NO3)2·6H2O (3.0 mmol). After stirred at room temperature for 60 s four pieces of nickel foam (the nominal size of one piece of nickel foam is 1.0 cm × 1.0 cm) were placed into above mixture solution and aged in the dark without any interference for different time (2 h, 12 h, 24 h, and 48 h). Finally, the obtained nickel foam-supported products were washed with deionized water followed by a drying treatment in an oven at 65°C for 12 h, and they were denoted as CoFe-PBA NS@NF-2, CoFe-PBA NS@NF-12, CoFe-PBA NS@NF-24 and CoFe-PBA NS@NF-48 on the basis of reaction time, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows peaks at 17.4°, 24.7°, 35.1° and 39.3° corresponding to (200), (220), (400) and (420) planes of CoFe-PBA, confirming pure CoFe-PBA phase besides NF peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3a showed the X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) pattern of the as-prepared CoFe-PBA NS@NF-24 composite. Except for the peaks belonged to the NF, four main peaks positioned at around 17.4, 24.7, 35.1 and 39.3° could be appreciably identified, which could correspond to (200), (220), (400) and (420) planes of CoFe-PBA, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows stronger signal peak intensity from unpaired electrons in CoFe-PBA compared to typical Co3[Fe(CN)6]2, suggesting existence of open metal centers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3c showed the electron spin resonance (ESR) spectra, from which it could be evidently seen the stronger signal peak intensity recorded from the unpaired electrons in our CoFe-PBA compared to the typical PBA, i.e., Co3[(Fe(CN)6]2, suggesting the existence of the open metal centers.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Co 2p and Fe 2p XPS spectra confirm divalent Co²⁺ and Fe²⁺ properties consistent with Co[Fe(CN)₅(NO)]·4H₂O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, both the high-resolution Co 2p and Fe 2p XPS spectra showed the divalent property (Fig. 3d and e), being consistent with previous report.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of ~70 m²/g with wide pore size distribution from 4-9 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results showed that the nanosheets in CoFe-PBA NS@NF-24 had a moderate BET surface area of ~70 m²g⁻¹ and displayed the wide pore size ranging from 4 - 9 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows average nanosheet thickness of about 5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, as a compelling evidence of the ultrathin feature of nanosheets, the atomic force microscopy (AFM) image was shown in Fig. 3g, and the corresponding line-scan profiles indicated that the average thickness of the nanosheets was about 5 nm (Fig. 3h).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows semitransparent feature, warped edges, and several layers of closely touched nanosheets; SAED confirms pure CoFe-PBA single crystal phase; HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.511 nm for (200) facet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the magnified TEM image also suggested that several layers of nanosheets were closely touched... Being in agreement with the XRD result, the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern recorded from the individual nanosheet area shows bright diffraction spots with cubically arranged shape, confirming the formation of pure CoFe-PBA phase... Nevertheless, the undamaged parts disclosed by high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) displayed clear lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of 0.511 nm, which could be indexed as the (200) facet of CoFe-PBA.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows uniform dispersion of metal species; elemental mapping confirms homogeneous distribution of Co, Fe, C, N, and O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image of representative CoFe-PBA nanosheet proclaimed that the metal species were uniformly dispersed on nanosheet... The elemental mapping result confirmed the homogeneous distribution of Co, Fe, C, N, and O elements within the nanosheet framework.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES shows atomic ratio of Fe:Co = 0.96:1 before catalysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Note that the molar ratio of Fe: Co determined by the inductively coupled plasma (ICP) was decreased from 0.96:1 before OER cycle to 0.22:1 after OER cycle.
